We normally experience music through sound. What happens when we turn the visual artwork surrounding music into data?

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)

# 15 albums arranged chronologically across 5 genres (3 each)
albums <- tibble(
  title = c(
    "Blue Train",
    "Kind of Blue",
    "Time Out",
    "Abbey Road",
    "Led Zeppelin IV",
    "The Dark Side of the Moon",
    "Thriller",
    "1999",
    "True Blue",
    "The Low End Theory",
    "Selected Ambient Works 85-92",
    "Illmatic",
    "Dig Your Own Hole",
    "Mezzanine",
    "Stankonia"

  artist = c(
    "John Coltrane",
    "Miles Davis",

    "The Beatles",
```

## Album Explorer

Explore album covers across genres and decades.

```{r}
#| label: album-grid
#| results: asis

cards <- albums |>
  pmap_chr(\(title, artist, genre, year, decade, cover_url) {
    paste0(
      '<div class="grid-card">',
      '<img src="', cover_url, '" alt="', htmltools::htmlEscape(title), '" loading="lazy">',
      '<div class="grid-info">',
      '<strong>', htmltools::htmlEscape(title), '</strong>',
      '<span>', htmltools::htmlEscape(artist), '</span>',
      '<small>', year, ' &bull; ', genre, '</small>',
      '</div></div>'
    )
  })

cat('<div class="album-grid">', cards, '</div>', sep = "\n")
```

```{=html}
<script>
  window.ALBUM_DATA = `r jsonlite::toJSON(albums)`;
</script>
<script src="timelapse.js"></script>
```
